Collection Description
This collection is an introduction to the [MongoDB Data API](https://www.mongodb.com/data-api/l). The Data API provides you with a REST-like access to your data in [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas), the database-as-a-service offering by MongoDB. You can find the full documentation on the MongoDB Data API on the [documentation website](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/api/data-api-resources/#data-api-resources). ## Getting Started To test out the MongoDB Data API collection, start by [creating a free MongoDB Atlas cluster](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/tutorial/deploy-free-tier-cluster/). Once you have a cluster, you can [fork this collection](https://www.postman.com/mongodb-devrel/workspace/mongodb-public/collection/17898583-25682080-e247-4d25-8e5c-1798461c7db4/fork) into your own workspace so you'll be able to use it with your own variables. Once you have a cluster up and running, [enable the Data API](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/api/data-api/#1.-enable-the-data-api). From the Atlas UI, copy the URL endpoint provided for the Data API, and paste the value in your URL_ENDPOINT collection variable. Still in the Atlas UI, create a new API key, copy the value and paste it in the API_KEY collection variable. With the [EJSON format](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/data-api/#extended-json-responses), you can benefit from MongoDB’s Extended JSON format, which preserves many data types that are normally not supported by JSON (such as ObjectID, Date, and more). For writes, the {{CONTENT_TYPE}} variable is required and can be set to either `json` or `ejson`. This variable is used by Postman in the *Content-Type* header. For reads, the Data API returns JSON by default, but can be changed to EJSON by setting the *Accept* header. You can set the {{CONTENT_TYPE}} variable to `json` or `ejson` to change the default behavior. Changing this variable will change the *Accept* header when Postman does a request to the Data API. The default content type returned by Atlas can also be changed in the Atlas Admin UI. Fill in the other variables with the appropriate values for your cluster, database, and collection names. You can now explore the various endpoints and see how to perform CRUD operations on your collection using the MongoDB Data API.

Kenny was very quick to respond to questions and provided info clearly. We liked that the apartment had Netflix already set up, and the kitchen was well-stocked with utensils if you want to save some money and cook for yourself. Bring your own food staples though, (salt, sugar, butter, etc) as there was no food in the apartment. Parking spot was easy to find, and we enjoyed the general feel of the place (brick walls, a good amount of light, big stack of clean towels). Our only real complaints were first, that the apartment is listed as 1.5 bathrooms, but there was only 1. As there were 4 of us, this wouldn't have been a deal breaker but we would have liked to know what to expect ahead of time. And second, the bed in the back bedroom was not very comfortable (front bedroom was fine, and no one slept in the middle bedroom so I can't speak for its comfort level). One of the fans did not work and another did not function as well as it should . There was not a third one. Light switches were hard to find and some of the lights did not work. \nThe main complaint is that they listed as an amenity, a parking space. This is not true. Fortunately, the manger was there when we arrived and very graciously got in my car and helped us find a public parking space that was good until we left. I will stay there again!"},{"_id":"267484586","date":"2018-05-21T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14284682","reviewer_id":"164658267","reviewer_name":"Jamie","comments":"Staying at the Wilder House is an experience. The history will grab you. The beauty will enthrall you. Peace will overcome you. The daily, intense rainbow will delight you. You will sleep deeply in the cool mountain air. The house will fulfill your every need. \n\nWhen you’re done with the hustle bustle, heavy traffic, crowded tourist spots, you come “home” to a home that is quiet, peaceful, breathtakingly beautiful. The view of Diamond Head will greet you every morning. The birds will amuse you and the gardens will occupy you for hours as you notice tropical beauty on tropical beauty. \n\nRead the book provided by Stanton and Bruce called “The Wilders of Waikiki .”  You will be immersed in the intricate intertwining of the Wilders into the workings and government of Hawaii, first with the royalty and then with the territorial government. You get swept up in the parties held at the house in the clouds. You realize how important the people that lived there were and now you are living there for your vacation. In this house you are a resident. A part of its history. Important to it living on by the energy you bring.\n\nI will come back to the Wilder House hoping it remembers my energy and welcomes me again. I’ll gladly drive up the mountain with its hair raising, hair pin turns and drop off cliffs. The higher you go, the more rain forest you twist through. You see bamboo, eucalyptus, orchids, vines and banyons seemingly holding up the forest canopy. It’s a world separated from the usual reality. \n\nI hope you decide to stay at the Wilder House. You will be very happy with the experience. It’s as far from a hotel room you could ever get.   ALOHA OE"},{"_id":"297990019","date":"2018-07-28T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14284682","reviewer_id":"38414545","reviewer_name":"Bunwoo","comments":"This place is unique with spacious rooms and areas for various activities. you would want to spend more time here to enjoy visiting with your friends and family. What impressed me the most was how thoughtful they were in putting the place together and making sure that it had EVERYTHING.  (The towels earned rave reviews and I have been \"encouraged\" to make similar upgrades to my own apartment.)  Great decor, too - tasteful, luxurious, homely, and varied: the rooms are each themed differently.  \r\n\r\nI know that Waianae has something of a poor reputation, but the immediate neighborhood is GREAT and feels like any high-class suburban area.  \r\n\r\nBefore booking, you do have to understand that it's located about 45 minutes outside of downtown Honolulu (traffic depending), so if you're not willing to make that drive then you should look for another unit, but for us this wasn't a downside - we LOVED our experience.  There are also beaches and hikes (Kaena Point) and snorkeling (Electric Beach may be the best place on the island and it's about 15 minutes south) and camping and a few restaurants closer to home if you decide you don't feel like it after you've arrived on the Island, and the home itself is just a terrific place to relax.\r\n\r\nI have stayed in a few of the major hotels in Waikiki, and this unit is so much better that you shouldn't hesitate at all - it's quieter, cleaner, much bigger and more comfortable, and a vastly better value.  Plus it comes with a parking space.\r\n\r\nThe hosts are also fantastic and they really cared about making sure that we had a great time.\r\n\r\nVery, VERY highly recommended. "},{"_id":"28655092","date":"2015-03-28T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"1915001","reviewer_id":"27714447","reviewer_name":"Mohammad","comments":"Our stay with Dulce was extremely pleasant. "},{"_id":"29284437","date":"2015-04-06T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"1915001","reviewer_id":"28133507","reviewer_name":"Matt","comments":"Very comfortable, fully furnished house with soft plush carpeting and A/C's in every room. 3 minute drive to beach, 10 minutes to Ko Olina/ Paradise Cove, 15 minutes to Target / Costco.\r\n\r\nWe're 4 guys, mid 30s professionals, living/working in beautiful Monterey CA who decided to travel to Hawaii to celebrate a birthday and visit an old friend. \r\n\r\nWe arrived in Honolulu Saturday morning and after picking up the car, eating lunch, and making a Target  run, we drove the 45 minutes to Waianae and checked-in. \r\n\r\nRick and family were already at the house when we arrived at 4pm where they promptly greeted us with warm smiles and traditional Hawaiian Lei's. Rick then spent a few minutes showing us the many amenities of the house (beach gear, towels, BBQ, etc.) followed by 20 minutes where we just chatted about the attractions in the area including the local artist that provided the amazing art hanging in the house. Rick is a fantastic source of information and gave us plenty of tips including one that saved us $250. \r\n\r\nAfter settling in we spent the next 8 days exploring all over the island, putting 700 miles on our rental car, but always returning in the evening to a nice comfortable home. This was ideal for us as we only had to grab towels, a cooler, and the gear we needed for the day. We could travel light, not worry about our luggage, and know there was an ice cold beer waiting at home (beer not provided). It was also great not worrying about packing too much clothes since we could do laundry in the evenings after a day of adventure. \r\n\r\nThe proximity to Ko Olina was also perfect as our preferred Luau and sailboat/snorkel tour were based out of here. There are 4 major resorts in Ko Olina so there's plenty to do there . We spent time at the Aulani Disney Resort and Ko Olina Lagoon. \r\n\r\nThe bottom line is that this house is perfect for those interested in getting out and exploring all corners of Oahu. If all you want is to lay on a beach then one of the many resorts would be a better choice. If you want a very comfortable, affordable, spacious base-camp to call home while you explore the island, then this place is perfect for you. \r\n"},{"_id":"29915394","date":"2015-04-14T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"1915001","reviewer_id":"7732876","reviewer_name":"Steve","comments":"Dulce and her family were awesome hosts. Éramos dos parejas y hemos pasado unos días estupendos. La casa está bien ubicada, a menos de 10 minutos caminando de la Plaza de Poveiros, en un barrio muy tranquilo.\nLa casa es espectacular, techos altos, grandes ventanales, arte por cada rincón y cada pared, silenciosa...Las camas nos resultaron comodísimas. En el piso de abajo está la cocina-comedor (perfectamente equipada), una sala que puede convertirse en habitación si se precisa, y un salón con acceso a un pequeño aseo, un balcón y unas escaleras que llevan a un jardín. En el piso de arriba están las dos habitaciones, una sala y el amplio baño. \nLuzia, la propietaria, nos recibió a la hora acordada. Fue muy amable con nosotros y nos dejó un pan riquísimo, vino, pasteles, fruta...además de recomendaciones de restaurantes y demás detalles para ayudarnos en nuestra estancia en Porto.\nLa comunicación con Luzia durante todo nuestro viaje fue muy fluida, preocupándose en todo momento por nuestra comodidad y teniendo detalles muy bonitos con nosotros, cosa que le agradecemos enormemente. \nEn resumidas cuentas, nos ha encantado la casa de Luzia y si volvemos a Porto seguro que repetiremos estancia, sin duda."},{"_id":"261938285","date":"2018-05-07T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"22396955","reviewer_id":"36338498","reviewer_name":"Jennifer","comments":"Unique house and location to experience Porto with all needs like public transport nearby."},{"_id":"264643617","date":"2018-05-14T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"22396955","reviewer_id":"55540121","reviewer_name":"Edwin","comments":"Luzia was a great host, collecting us from the airport and baking us a delicious cake. It’s a beautiful and comfortable home with a huge lanai, hot tub, sauna, outdoor shower and peek a boo ocean view through the lush foliage. The farm environment was perfect for us although the odd rooster confused a bright moon with dawn on occasion LOL.  We found the location great with short drives to a grocery store, fruit stands, snorkel spots/beaches and excellent restaurants.  Initially it felt like our neighbours were very close (we live on a ranch with a 1 mile access road to give you some perspective)  however we found we had excellent privacy and minimal noise. Listening to the crickets, frogs and the waves on the shores below in the evening and at night was wonderful.  Our hosts were great, very accommodating and anxious to ensure we had everything we needed. We had  fresh fruit on arrival as well as more offerings half way through our trip. There is a great little stash of beach equipment we were free to use including snorkel equipment, chairs, cooler etc available on a first come basis.  The beds were comfortable and linens were great. WiFi was excellent. Kitchen equipment, stove, fridge, dishwasher all great. We made fantastic smoothies everyday.  For us, this was a perfect place to stay. Oh yes, the 2 friendly kitties were an added bonus along with a small supply of free eggs from free range wild chickens laid on the lanai.  Avoid Gypsea Gelato - it’s addictive. Overall the experience and the house was great!!"},{"_id":"165662747","date":"2017-07-01T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"5249793","reviewer_id":"8805609","reviewer_name":"Valerie","comments":"Our group of 5 adults stayed here at the end of June. The size of the space was great. We used all three bedrooms and both bathrooms. The lanai is beautiful especially in the early hours of the morning. Fair warning that there is a big mosquito issue in this area of the island from the consistent sun/rain/overcast each day and lush greenery. We did not get to enjoy the lanai too much for that reason. Simin provides lots of mosquito candles but the mosquitoes are vicious. Our husbands tuffed it out and grilled battling the mosquitos. Simin's book is very helpful at explaining but maybe add to the listing description too.\n\nThe house is on a roof water catchment system which we didn't remember seeing in the listing description. Luckily we had plenty of rain to make sure we didn't run out of water for showers, dishes, etc. Simin's book explains the system. Drinking water can be bought/refilled at the market. Also, trash has to be taken to the local dump 15 minutes away. This was a bit difficult with our group and rental car size. We were not able to take trash on our last day and Simin was kindly good with that. \n\nThe driveway and general area of this part of the island is steep, with curving highways. Be prepared to return at reasonable hours before sunset as the highway is also very curvy and dark. Also, restaurants, gas, and market are about a 20-30 minute drive away. They do close early so plan ahead. We enjoyed the Choice Market selection and Keoki's Ono Fish n Chips is the best! \n\nKona is a good hour drive. Hilo closer to 2 hours. Volcano park 1.5 hours. 30 minutes or less to most of the coffee farms. \n\nThe drive to the pebble beach is very steep. I don't recommend walking unless you are in very, very good shape. The area of the house is very safe and also secluded. The avocado tree in front is beautiful, \n\nWindow coverings in the future would be nice. We often watched movies at night and are from the City, so it felt about odd to not have curtains. But the windows do let in a lot of natural light during the day. The master room faces the lanai. If you have a big group, privacy can be an issue. \n\nMore fans would be nice. We bought our own. We had a few very warm days and lost power for we think about 30 minutes but luckily we were already heading to the beach. We kept windows and doors closed to keep out the bugs. They did often sneak in through the screens if not closed.\n\nOverall, we enjoyed our adventurous stay and appreciated Simin's communication and book. We definitely had a memorable stay and the house was a perfect size for our group of five. Thanks, Simin.\n\n "},{"_id":"195988706","date":"2017-09-21T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"5249793","reviewer_id":"34007174","reviewer_name":"Parees","comments":"The host canceled this reservation 9 days before arrival. Neighborhood was friendly and helpful!"},{"_id":"284652842","date":"2018-07-01T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"5249793","reviewer_id":"87918396","reviewer_name":"Sally","comments":"This place is a very solid pick. When you first drive up you might be confused because all you see at first is a very small building. That's just the gym! The whole house is quite large and is down below the workout shed. The porch is quite large and gorgeous. The first thing we did when we arrived was to crack some beers and lounge in the hammock and porch swing which look out on the water less than a mile below. The porch is surrounded by various colorful, flowering trees and avocado trees. It feels very lush. The vegetation completely blocks any visual of the neighbors so it took me a while realize there was a house on one side of us. We could hear them sometimes but it wasn't annoying. The house has a lot of extras that made our vacation special. The grill was crucial - we used it almost every night and it made dinners so easy and delicious, and clean up was a breeze. We ate out on the porch every night, and then played cards or just talked. The fridge is full of condiments so you probably won't need to worry about shelling out for long-lasting extras like ketchup, mayo, mustard, hot sauce, etc. There is a drip coffee maker AND a french press for coffee snobs. Beyond the kitchen, there is a lot of beach/water gear: Several sets of snorkels with fins; two beach chairs (one is a little worse for wear but usable); two beach umbrellas, a cooler and beach towels. You might need to sort through the snorkel gear a bit to make sure you're getting the good stuff, since a couple of the masks are broken. A couple of us still rented gear at Snorkel Bob's because we wanted to go several times and couldn't get a good fit with any of the masks at the house, but two of us just used the house gear the whole time. I wasted space in my suitcase on beach towels, since this place had solid ones on offer. Most notable of all, though, was the friendly and communicative demeanor of Simin and her property manager, Martin. Soon after my reservation, Simin let me know that the sink in the guest bathroom wasn't working, though she hoped to have it repaired before we arrived. Shortly before we arrived, she let me know that the sink was still broken, and offered us a generous discount without any negotiation on my part. I received a text message from Martin on the day we were supposed to arrive, and then he was refilling the water tank at the property when we arrived, and was helpful and friendly. Then, toward the end of our visit, I realized that I had overbooked our stay, so we were paying for an extra night after our flight back to the mainland! I sent Simin a message and she immediately responded, refunding me that night of our stay. She didn't..."},{"_id":"329423144","date":"2018-09-28T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"5249793","reviewer_id":"18738949","reviewer_name":"Ashley","comments":"I had mixed feelings about this place. The outdoor patio would have been a great place to spend a good amount of our time, but the mosquitoes were out 24/7. Bug spray/citronella didn't help, those guys were vicious! So despite the patio being one of the main reasons we booked the house, we couldn't really use it :( Also, everything in the kitchen has a thin coating of dirt/grime. All the pots/pans/utensils/shelves etc were dirty.  Another downside to our stay was there was a leak prior to our arrival that caused us limited use of the second bathroom and one of the bedrooms. Martin was kind enough to warn us prior to our arrival, but it wasn't a desirable situation. The last thing, which isn't much of a criticism, but just unexpected was the windows in the master bedroom don't have shades, so be prepared to get up with the sun (and the neighbors roosters and dogs). Value-wise, not great compared to other rentals we've had in the area, especially since two rooms were out of order, but that's obliviously subjective. A big plus to this place is that it is just a few steps from Nathan Road. About 3 blocks away from jordan station. The place was very clean and spacious. There are restaurants, department stores and convenience store nearby if you need to get anything. My only comment during our stay was the fact that shampoo for bathing and laundry soap to wash the dishes was not adequate. I raised this issue on the first night as they visited the unit but their only reply to me was it can last for the duration of our stay. Well it did not. It ran out in the first 2 days fortunately we brought our own. I understand they are not a hotel but with the amount that they charge, they should at least refill this for the next guests that would be staying there. Refilling will not in any way hurt their income. There were only 2 sets of fork & spoon. The place could accommodate 10 guests and this is not enough. We were 4 adults. Although there were chopsticks, if you are not used to using them then its difficult to use. We asked numerous questions.  Instructions from the airport to his property were very clear.  We were greeted upon arrival to a nearby bus stop and escorted to the unit.  A warm introduction and tour was included.  \r\n\r\nThe accommodations were spacious.  There is no heater in the unit, but blankets were provided. Our visit was in February and although cold and rainy outside, the home was suitable.  Late spring and summer are warmer months.  Yau was very accommodating as he addressed building issues (issues beyond his control) as well as any one could.  \r\n\r\nThe unit has the basics.  Nothing fancy and everything works.  There's a cook top, place settings to serve and cook a home cooked meal.  Refrigerator was of an appropriate size.  We didn't find a grocery store in the area but there was one one metro stop away. \r\n\r\nThe unit is very convenient and 2 blocks north of the Jordan MTR station.  \r\n\r\nOn the negative side, the bathroom could have been cleaner.  Moisture control is difficult in a windowless room.  The tub had mildew and the floors were difficult to keep dry. Cleaning supplies and mop were accessible.  Yau had numerous pairs of slippers available.  Slippers and a mop fixed this issue.  I mention this one negative for fairness to Yau and future guests.  If you are expecting a level of polish typical of a franchise hotel in a western metropolis, you will be disappointed here.  This unit, despite this one issue, is a great value considering the location, price and size.   You will be able to pay more for other accommodations, but get less value.  We stayed at Yau's for five days in a group of 7 adults and two toddlers.  We were comfortable for the few hours per day that we were \"home\" between trips all over town.  Did I say it was only 2 blocks from the MTR?\r\n\r\nFiguratively speaking, our stay was like staying with extended family members who were in college; the place had a functional minimalism.  At the same time it felt like Yau communicated and addressed issues to please as though accountable to a mutual family member.  I would stay at this property again, but after asking to stay at Grandma's.  "},{"_id":"64034716","date":"2016-02-29T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"7564603","reviewer_id":"44344933","reviewer_name":"Maf","comments":"- Great location, prompt response from host, friendly cleaner, very spacious, comfortable, fast internet connection, no curfew \n- Building is under renovation so it was noisy and appearance is not appealing, there was only one elevator which was small and covered with plywood\n- Overall it was a nice stay "},{"_id":"64419911","date":"2016-03-04T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"7564603","reviewer_id":"47350807","reviewer_name":"David","comments":"Good location and service! There are two airport buses A21 along Nathan Rd and A22 on Jordan Rd (we used this when we left to avoid using the underground pedestrian passage to cross Nathan Rd.... plus the A22 bus stop has cover, it was raining...) Also, a dry cleaner/laundry by the pound place one street up that has good and fast service - only 1 day to turn around dry cleaning!\n\nFood Food everywhere!\nHK style cafe... chinese restaurants.. congee shop (very busy, very good!).. japanese .. Western... starbucks... etc all within walking distance.\n\nSpacious rooms and lounge. Included wifi was OK (we did have to reset once for it to work). Shower pressure was strong, but drainage a bit slow... so you gotta be conservative with water usage or risk overflowing.. recommend guests to turn tap off to lather!\n\nBYO towels and toiletries... we even bought our own toilet rolls as we were only left one new roll for three people / three nights' stay. We also BYO extra towel for bath mat. \n\nLinen was a bit questionable. Stained linen..hmm.. \n\nA rack or even multiple hooks in the rooms would have been more convenient. As we needed places to hang up our evening dresses and suits for the wedding we were attending.\n\nToilet died on night of Day 2. Cistern will not fill up... water just flows continuously .. pressing flush button did nothing. We reported the issue to host/management. We then then told to call another colleague - who then told us nothing could be done until the next morning and wr should try to flush with the shower head or pot of water. Nobody contacted us to follow up nor came to fix the toilet up until we checked out and left."},{"_id":"67816681","date":"2016-03-31T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"7564603","reviewer_id":"5928318","reviewer_name":"Lausanne","comments":"The apartment was exactly as described on the listing... it was huge by HK standards - perfect for 3 single females, a 3 night stopover and a whole lot of luggage. The information provided to get from the airport to the apartment was accurate and we were met promptly by a lovely gentleman who showed us to the apartment.  The apartment was clean and had everything we needed.  The kitchen facilities were basic but we only ate breakfast in so it suited our needs perfectly. We always use hotels and serviced apartments for our holiday trips. The apartment itself is well renovated and the location is great, however there are a couple of misses that we'd like to point out in this review. COMMUNICATION: During our last night, we sent a message to Matthew and asked permission if we can check out at around 12-1pm as we are sending our family to the airport. He replied that we are only allowed to leave our bags in the apartment until 2pm because they need to clean the house. At 9 AM before going to the airport, we neatly placed our belongings including our souvenirs in the living room next to the TV. At 10:19 AM I even gave Matthew a call that we are on our way back to the house from the airport and we will be arriving back before 12 noon. We returned to the apartment on time to pick our belongings. We were in shock to find out that the cleaner/co-host Chris THREW AWAY our souvenir bag in the rubbish bin outside the house!!! The souvenirs are two fragile wax model of our hands from Madame Tussauds which we had made for our 6th wedding anniversary!!! It was kept nicely in a box and a Madame Tussauds souvenir tote bag. We could not comprehend how Chris could mistook it for rubbish! To make it worse, it was raining during that day and the rubbish bin was wet and dirty. This Chris kept making excuses and blamed Matthew that he wasn't informed that we will leave our belongings. However even if he was not informed by Matthew, he still has NO RIGHT to touch the guests' belongings and more so throw it to the rubbish bin. Clearly, communication was not the only issue here but also the lack of common sense. CLEANLINESS: 1.) The basement bedroom has a strong musty odour on the day of arrival and smells like sewage everytime we go back to the apartment after spending the day on tour. They only have a Glen 20 spray which did not mask the odour. 2.) On day of arrival, there is a lock of hair (possibly from the previous guests) in the kitchen trash bin. There are also left over drinks (soft drinks and juices) inside the fridge. 3.) Upon arrival, we strictly followed the No Shoes policy in the house straight away. However, as Matthew was touring us inside...he had his shoes ON while walking around the house which made the floor dirty. 4.) Dusty tables beside the bed and underneath the TV in the basement bedroom. 5.) My brother saw cockroaches in the Attic bedroom on two occasions. 6.) The sheets on the first floor bedroom smelled nice, however, the sheets on the Attic bedroom smelled musty...."},{"_id":"210503159","date":"2017-11-09T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"9516607","reviewer_id":"131981365","reviewer_name":"Jamie","comments":"Great area and a very cool place!"},{"_id":"211711154","date":"2017-11-14T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"9516607","reviewer_id":"32196809","reviewer_name":"Nichola","comments":"Great place for a group - six of us fit very comfortably. The young fledgling Shearwaters leave the nest and fly till they see moonlight or starlight reflected in the ocean. They then will land and rest for the night to begin their life as a denizen of the sea. So,...the open and dark skies at the house, not only assist the Shearwaters, but make for wonderful stargazing at the property. The house was spacious and airy and adorned in true Hawaiian style with gorgeous wood floors and furniture, and large lanais on every side. Morning and afternoons we spent lounging at the pool or on the main lanai overlooking the beautiful gardens, or wandering the many pathways near the house to explore the exotic trees and plants and smell the enchanting orchids. This is a true paradise away from the bustle of the beaches and Kona town, which are just moments away. We appreciated the seclusion and privacy after a busy day at Hapuna Beach, especially the outdoor shower and the large sliding wood doors opening the house to the cool air.  The gourmet kitchen had everything we could possibly need including high-end appliances, and with Costco and several other stores just minutes away it was easy to grab some groceries at the end of the day and enjoy relaxing cocktails and dinners on the lanai while watching the sunset. The house itself is spotless and the beds were dreamy; we slept well each night with the windows wide open. The library was a special place for quiet moments to peruse books on exploration and adventure, and gave a warm feel to the house and a personal connection to the owner. Hard to believe a better place can be found that is so close to town and the beaches and the airport, yet just moments up the hill is complete seclusion and relaxation. This is a true paradise and highly recommended for anyone looking for a luxury garden retreat!"},{"_id":"224868128","date":"2018-01-04T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14758081","reviewer_id":"6931604","reviewer_name":"Anita","comments":"This is a truly unique and special home. "},{"_id":"306622950","date":"2018-08-12T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14758081","reviewer_id":"39089422","reviewer_name":"Ariana","comments":"This entire property is breathtaking! Perfect amount of space for my family of 6 and a gorgeous, lush setting for getting ready for my destination wedding in Kailua-Kona. It's ~15 minutes from downtown and at a higher elevation, so even though there was no AC, it was a solid 10 degrees cooler than the notoriously hot and humid coast in early August. Host was super responsive, informative, and accommodating and was quick about fixing a broken sliding door on the lanai. Tons of space (the grounds were especially big) with extra cots/sleeping pads that were actually pretty comfortable. And the plants/foliage! Definitely a highlight for us. It was so beautiful, and the more remote location gave the property a serene feel.\n\nTip: wear bug spray! Lots of mosquitoes, which really shouldn't have surprised us at all given how tropical the climate is. In addition, don't be surprised if you see some other bugs crawling around because that's pretty much inevitable.\n\nOverall, we absolutely loved our stay here and highly recommend it. Has a great country feel to it, with roosters crowing in the early dawn. The place is gated, which is a huge plus. Parking spots are provided. The location is in North Shore super close to Haleiwa and all the beautiful beaches. I would suggest renting a vehicle to get to all your destinations. \n\nHost:\nThe owner/host lives on site which, to me, was super convenient because he was able to answer questions immediately or provide us with things that were missing. He was very accommodating. The dogs are also super friendly. My baby wasn't even afraid of them. \n\nPlace:\nOur place was clean and inviting. The only downfall I would say was that there was no AC, but the ceiling fans made up for it. It's all hardwood flooring. Each room had closets. The host even provided us with a foam cooler, beach towels, and a beach umbrella for use. We made our own breakfast daily and ate it on the balcony while staring into the beautiful view. The furniture was comfy. The decoration was modern and matched very well with the furniture. The showers do work but difficult to figure out and once you get it, it's fairly simple. There are fruit trees on site that the host allowed us to pick at freely. The mangoes were delicious! \n\nAll in all, we enjoyed our stay very much and would recommend to everyone."},{"_id":"230976535","date":"2018-01-29T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15285714","reviewer_id":"27527539","reviewer_name":"Paula","comments":"We loved this place. This place feels safe, don't have to worry about leaving stuff in the place with the doors unlocked. I loved the dog adira, it kept coming over and saying hi the whole time. The other dog was really shy. Really has an amazing view out of the porch. I would look this place up first among any other options when ever back in Oahu. Also I loved the chickens/ roosters they are very good at making sure you get up on time in the morning. This helped to maximize our time and do more activities as they never miss their 5am wake up calls, even when there was a tropical storm hitting they still did the job.\n\nThings that could be done better: A.C. I know the listing says no AC so you can't be mad at that. It got super hot and humid while there and the fans can only do so much. Maybe they should invest in a portable swamp cooler that rolls around for the summer time. I'd even pay more if that's what it would take. \n\nBugs, bugs, and more bugs. I understand it's Hawaii , everything is green and it's country. So I can live with the bugs. It is a little nerve wrecking when you hop in the shower and there's just a lizard staring you down on the wall, or a cockroach that hides inside your jacket. Other than that it's to be expected as it's country, and I'd still come back 100 times over.\n\nThe host really should include instructions somewhere on how to turn on the shower. that might be the norm in Hawaii but I've never seen anything like it, and after reading the reviews looks like others have had the same issue. However the host is a short phone call away and you'll have it figured out. \n\nThat being said this is a perfect listing, and is soooooo much better than staying in Waikiki. Hapuna Beach is a little further-maybe 15 minutes-but so worth it-one of the nicest beaches we have ever been to. Make sure you do your grocery shopping on the way, either in Waimea if coming from that direction, or Kailua-Kona, because there is nothing nearby. The listing is clear that there is car and truck noise from the road. This is true. But it is the only noise. Otherwise it is very quiet and peaceful. There is less traffic after 9:30pm and it only starts again around 5am. We slept with the windows open for a breeze and I closed them and turned on the a/c when the traffic started at dawn. The a/c really mutes the noise. I am a very light sleeper and I slept fine. The garden is quite big, the kids had fun playing in it. There is a hose out back to rinse off feet and beach stuff. The decor is pretty, it has a very hawaiian beach vibe. The beds are very comfortable, we slept very well. The shower has good water pressure. We recommend this place, just don't expect to eat out in restaurants or pick something up. The living area is old style vaulted which is lovely. The place is dated, but it feels island-y so that really isn't a problem. Coming from ultra modern San Francisco it is quite a change, but a welcome one. The walk to beach is about 10 minutes and the local beach is Kahekili beach, which is great for snorkeling (though there are better). The beach is much better than Kaanapali (which is frankly awful) and is a great place to be based. It was never crowded. As for the house: There were ample boogie boards (no waves so we didn't use them). There were ample masks and snorkels for adults and kids (we didn't use because we brought our own) and a pair of fins (we had our own). Plenty of towels as well. There was a small beach umbrella, which does the trick for two, but we brought our own sand anchor and would recommend either your own umbrella with anchor or purchasing one. There were also a couple of coolers (which we used) and various other items. We did bring our own water shoes and those are essential for kids and less confident swimmers. The house had a fully stocked kitchen including many basic ingredients (no olive oil, but we left our extra bottle). There was also trash bags and dishwasher soap, as well as laundry pods (we never did laundry). Bathrooms has soap and hand soap as well. Shopping was really limited to groceries, which was incredibly useful. Carol had a bottle of wine for us when we arrived. Parking was easy and right next door. We used the car to go to farther beaches and the Safeway (about 10 minutes away). The lanai was very pleasant with a good gas BBQ. All switches were thoroughly explained with sticky labels (actually quite a good idea). The TV and entertainment area was lacking. No way to connect to the dated stereo system (bring your own UE speaker for hanging out). And the TV channels on DISH were not HD (funny how poor the picture quality was until HD). Also no premium channels and the only way to watch movies was a DVD player. So no movie nights here. A couple of issues. The proximity to the highway was just loud enough to be noticeable but not enough to disturb sleep. The windows are old style glass slats which don't do a good job of noise damping or insulation, but do a good job of airing the house out during the night. There was AC but we don't like AC and didn't need it during out trip. Daytime high inside was 84 and overnight that dropped to 80. AC usually causes someone to get an earache so this is a blessing. The sprinkler woke us up a couple of times. Carol was an excellent host. The pictures really don’t do it justice! The kitchen was well-appointed and had everything we needed to cook many meals, and there was plenty of counter space. The dining area was very nice and had plenty of room as well. The living area had the most wondeful, cozy sofas. The layout of the main living area was great - since there were several seating areas, the teenagers could each have their own space while still being together with the adults. I also appreciated the little touches like the ceiling fans and stereo already being on when we arrived, that was very welcoming. The decor is somewhat modern with a vintage Hawaiian feel - the perfect combination. Bedrooms and bathrooms were nicely sized and in good shape. Das Apartment ist charmant, die Möbel schon etwas mitgenommen, aber das passt insgesamt ins Bild von Porto und macht den Reiz aus. Die Lage ist super, genau am Duoro. Es gibt Strassenmusik bis in den späten Abend und auch morgens geht's früh los mit fröhlichen Lärm von der Flusspromenade. Nichts also für Leute, die es ruhig brauchen! Die Lage ist wirklich exklusiv und tröstet über den recht teuren Mietpreis. Im Umfeld gibt es typische Touri-Fallen, wo alles doppelt kostet, aber gleichzeitig findet man auch sehr nette kleine Bars, in der man chillig und günstig frühstücken oder generell lecker essen kann. Die Stadt ist klein genug, um sich schnell zurechtzufinden und groß genug, um immer wieder neues zu entdecken. Wir waren zu dritt (50, 25, 20 Jahre) und haben die Zeit wirklich genossen. We have a well stocked supermarket that is open from 8am to 8pm.  Bundeena also has: chemist, newsagent, petrol station, resident doctor, ambulance station, fire station.  We are lucky to have a selection of cafes for those times you just want to kick back and look at the view and recently a newly opened restaurant.  We have a local bowling club that also has a restaurant. The name Bundeena is an aboriginal word meaning “noise like thunder” and when you hear the waves lap up against the white sand its easy to understand why. On Bundeena's southern edge, footsteps of the people who walked before us echo across the land. On the beach and in the bush, there’s hidden evidence of a life well-lived… you simply need to know where to look. Ferry timetable can be found by a search for Cronulla Ferries. To get here, the car journey is approx 25 mins from the Pacific Highway turn off at Sutherland/Loftus. Le jardin est un vrai bonheur. Bref, mes enfants étaient vraiment ravis et nous aussi. \r\nCaroline et Thierry sont des propriétaires chaleureux, disponibles et prevenants, un gentil présent nous attendait à notre arrivée. We liked having the piano to play on, too!\r\n\r\nThe kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms, and laundry room are all well equipped (as befitting a European-style kitchen, the coffee maker is a French press), and the giant windows facing out back from upstairs and downstairs are fantastic. We appreciated having the gas grill to use out on the deck and the private back yard (though our kids were likely a bit noisy for the back yards all next to one another!).\r\n\r\nThe location could not be better! The house is on a quiet residential side street in the hip neighborhood of Le Plateau--it felt like French Brooklyn. It's a very short walk to the Mont-Royal metro stop and on the way home from the metro it's easy to stop at the supermarket en route back to the house to pick up whatever you need for dinner. There are also tons of low-key options when it comes to eating out, especially with kids. There are two Second Cup locations within blocks from the house--like a French Canadian Starbucks and our go-to coffee break spot. Also, there are two playgrounds nearby, and one is next to a public pool.\r\n\r\nHaving the metro nearby was excellent as nearly everything we did was no more than four or five stops away. We drove up via New York State and we were a little nervous about city street parking, but in the summer at least it was always easy to find parking on days you had to move the car for street cleaning. Bondi Beach must be its sister city times two. As a bunch of aged birdwatchers we didn't really fit in but felt comfortable and accepted anyway. Lots of shops and good restaurants within easy walking distance, and the beach is just as close. There's even a funky little nine hole golf course close by. It's perched on a cliff that overlooks the ocean and has million dollar views.\n\nThe house worked well for five adults (one couple and three others) and was clean and well appointed. There are even cookbooks displayed in the kitchen in case you wanted to get adventurous. One of the bedrooms is in a guesthouse in the back yard and it was a nice place for the couple to sleep and be apart form the others. Be prepared for visiting bugs, though.\n\nBelieve Cat when she says that you won't be able to park inside the gate without a high clearance vehicle but you will be able to park in the driveway if your car is on the small side. We had a minivan that was simply too big to allow for pedestrians pushing baby strollers to get by. Parking on the street is for two hours only and the nearest long-term free parking is s few blocks away. Remember to always leave space between you and the next car as locals seem to have no issue with pinning you in if you don't. \n\nCat was great about communicating with us. Classificado como Património Mundial pela UNESCO, o centro da cidade é repleto de referências importantes que celebram a sua longa história e tradições, como a Catedral do século 12, com o seu soberbo altar de prata. Encante-se com os azulejos azuis e brancos que adornam a Estação de São Bento, e tire uma fotografia na Avenida dos Aliados, no coração do centro histórico da cidade. Descubra ainda outros lugares de destaque, como a Livraria Lello e o Café Majestic. Pare para explorar o mercado típico do Bolhão, admire os monumentos da Praça da Batalha, a emblemática Torre e Igreja dos Clérigos do século 18, e os jardins românticos do Palácio de Cristal. The renovations are really impressive - gorgeous stone walls, lovely woodwork, all perfectly clean and new looking. The beds were comfortable and the three of us (my two sisters and I) slept well there. It was great having three separate bedrooms, and two bathrooms. Really you could sleep about 8 people there if you wanted to, with the fold out couch on the second floor and the trundle bed in the upper room. We didn't cook there (the restaurant food is so good in Porto!) so I can't comment on the function of those facilities, but the kitchen is lovely to be in. The location is perfect - away from the noise of the river but easy walking distance. One warning - if you have a car, you need to figure out some sort of arrangement for parking. You pay 2 Euros per 2 hours to park on the street between 8 and 6, and you can't buy several hours at once. We got a 12 Euro ticket, but it actually seemed like a good deal for a day's worth of parking. Now we just have to figure out how to pay it! Everything has been thought of, from hats and repellant to hooks to hang out your wet beach towels. We will definitely be back. "},{"_id":"10075406","date":"2014-01-28T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"1714235","reviewer_id":"11593219","reviewer_name":"Julian","comments":"If you are seeking a charmingly rustic, secluded getaway to a cottage located twenty metres from a stunning protected beach; look no further.\r\n\r\nGetting to the house is a boating adventure directly from Palm Beach (either by the ferry, the friendly local boat house, or the water taxi). Not being able to drive to the house is a nice removal from the mundane, however make sure you pack accordingly.\r\n\r\nThe main sandstone cottage is designed to effortlessly entertain large or small groups of people. The generous outdoor setting is nicely accompanied by extra deck chairs and umbrellas.\r\n\r\nRichard and Claudia have very tastefully arranged the homely living interiors and bedrooms. The tree-house (bedroom and bathroom), removed from the main cottage, is fantastic and you are treated to a stunning elevated view to the East. Watching sunrise over the ocean from the comfort of  bed is pretty special.\r\n\r\nThe quiet location means sleeping with the doors open to the sound of gentle waves is a must, and the house is well stocked with mosquito coils to make the pests don't interrupt.\r\n\r\nThe recently renovated kitchen contains everything needed for cooking, and is complemented by the large BBQ outside.\r\n\r\nThere are walking trails nearby which can take you to the West Head lookout, Aboriginal Archaeological sites, and tiny beaches dotted around the headland.\r\n\r\nAll-in-all, a very pleasant stay, and we look forward to any opportunity to return."},{"_id":"10184416","date":"2014-02-04T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"1714235","reviewer_id":"11561171","reviewer_name":"Luka","comments":"Hands down one of the nicest places i've ever stayed in. The house is nestled in the bush with frangipani trees everywhere & plenty of ample space to relax or entertain guests. I'll be back for sure!"},{"_id":"10224810","date":"2014-02-07T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"1714235","reviewer_id":"7432323","reviewer_name":"Grace","comments":"We had a great stay at Richard's House. It is located on the inner side (not ocean side) of Kamehameha Highway. However, a quick cross of the highway at the driveway and a 3-5 min. walk and you are at Sunset Beach. You cannot see (or hear) the ocean from the house but it is hard to be the location. Ted’s Bakery is just down the highway, about a 4 min. walk as well. We enjoyed numerous meals there and the food is top quality!  Nice to have that so close. We stayed on the top level of the house. It was nice to have a personal bedroom for each of the three of us. We definitely appreciated the space. Amenities are basic but what we needed. Food cannot be left out as the ants will come. There is no A/C. It is best to not be in the house from say noon till sundown as it will be quite hot. However, opening the windows and bringing in the evening air is sufficient (we stayed the first week of November.) The occasional rain showers also helped to mediate the heat inside. Roosters begin their morning chatter around 4:30 am. Earplugs are a must if you are used to a more quiet sleeping environment. We had a few leaks in the roof on a day when the rains were heavier. We just moved the sofa out of the drip line and all was fine. We drove a lot around the island and this home was a great starting place for our day trips. Would definitely recommend this home for a stay in the North Shore."},{"_id":"405854256","date":"2019-01-27T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"4294289","reviewer_id":"229760840","reviewer_name":"Whitney","comments":"Great spot on the North Shore. The person sleeping there felt bad using up what little was left so we just shared back and forth every day.  A little inconvenient.  For such an elegant place one expects the small amenities to be standard in each bath.\nBottom line it's a great location and a stylish, comfortable home. Desmond's house is generally clean (if a bit dated) and conveniently situated to transportation, groceries, shopping, a gym, and a park.  Desmond himself is quick to respond to any questions sent. And the price presented a pretty compelling value for a family or group of 5+ people visiting NYC on a tight budget who don't need anything fancy. \n\nHowever, there was a bad. Everything was going fine UNTIL...\nDesmond and I agreed my family and I could stay an extra night since the house was available. However on that final night, a stranger I had never seen before barged into the house from the basement apartment while we were upstairs getting ready for bed. I ran downstairs to investigate and saw a completely naked and extremely intoxicated man had walked through the house to sit on the back deck off the dining room, barely conscious . I confronted him and he got startled and ran off through the back yard. I thought he was an intruder until I turned around and realized he had entered the house from the basement door which was flung wide open. I closed it but quickly realized there was no padlock or way to secure the door. \n\nUpon calling Desmond he said the man was \"a friend who sometimes stays with him\" in the downstairs apartment, and assured me it was a mixup. My wife and I were in complete shock at the experience and had to round up our things and our sleeping children at 11:00PM to go stay somewhere else because we could not stay under those circumstances with no padlock on the door to the basement apartment and a possible naked alcoholic staying below us. \n\nDesmond apologized for the confusion but I feel that people need to know that if you stay here you are potentially sharing your living space with anyone that might be downstairs with no way of locking the access door or ensuring privacy. At no point prior did Desmond tell us there was a guest downstairs, much less a naked alcoholic. I would never stay at Desmond's house again, and honestly the experience has us questioning whether we will ever use a home sharing service again."},{"_id":"202049859","date":"2017-10-09T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"7246903","reviewer_id":"32683151","reviewer_name":"Geoffray","comments":"Très bon logement pour les familles. It is locked on the other side so you cannot secure the house.\n\nOn our last day, we were eating lunch with colleagues when an aggressive man from downstairs (who apparently owns the house) burst in through the front door and accused my colleagues of being hookers! Desmond arrived on site and sided with his neighbour and aggressively forced us to leave the property. We were shocked and were worried for our well being so we left within ten minutes. Desmond then accused my colleagues of being \"transexual hookers\" who \"must have brought the bed bugs\" to the house... ( he sent this message to us through Airbnb)\n\nOur experience at this property is NOT UNIQUE however. Please see Eric's review from September 2017:  \n\n\n\"Everything was going fine UNTIL... First the good. Desmond's house is generally clean (if a bit dated) and conveniently situated to transportation, groceries, shopping, a gym, and a park. Desmond himself is quick to respond to any questions sent. And the price presented a pretty compelling value for a family or group of 5+ people visiting NYC on a tight budget who don't need anything fancy. However, there was a bad. Everything was going fine UNTIL... Desmond and I agreed my family and I could stay an extra night since the house was available. However on that final night, a stranger I had never seen before barged into the house from the basement apartment while we were upstairs getting ready for bed. I ran downstairs to investigate and saw a completely naked and extremely intoxicated man had walked through the house to sit on the back deck off the dining room, barely conscious . I confronted him and he got startled and ran off through the back yard. I thought he was an intruder until I turned around and realized he had entered the house from the basement door which was flung wide open. I closed it but quickly realized there was no padlock or way to secure the door. Upon calling Desmond he said the man was \"a friend who sometimes stays with him\" in the downstairs apartment, and assured me it was a mixup. My wife and I were in complete shock at the experience and had to round up our things and our sleeping children at 11:00PM to go stay somewhere else because we could not stay under those circumstances with no padlock on the door to the basement apartment and a possible naked alcoholic staying below us. Desmond apologized for the confusion but I feel that people need to know that if you stay here you are potentially sharing your living space with anyone that might be downstairs with no way of locking the access door or ensuring privacy. At no point prior did Desmond tell us there was a guest downstairs, much less a naked alcoholic. I would never stay at Desmond's house again, and honestly the experience has us questioning whether we will ever use a home sharing service again.\"\n\n\n\n\nWe were very disappointed because our trip to NY was very successful apart from this crazy incident."},{"_id":"408138546","date":"2019-02-03T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"7246903","reviewer_id":"7027682","reviewer_name":"Bethany","comments":"We had a great stay at Desmond's -- he met me in person for check in and showed me around the townhouse (which looks exactly as pictured) even though I arrived late in the evening. Loved it. We went to celebrate retirements, birthdays, relax and enjoy each others company and this complex provided us such an ideal opportunity to do so compared to the often crowded hotel resorts. This C1 villa has absolutely everything you need including heaps of beach gear in garage. We didn't want to spend $'s eating out each night and the really well appointed kitchen and BBQ allowed us to cook our own meals when we wished.  C1 is 10 metres from one of the the complexes 2 pools. Queens Market Place over road and Kings up the road, golf clubs in walking distance and ample walking opportunities. The community is compact from the Waikaloa Villas at one end to the Hilton Resort at  the other. The WBV's provide a pass to the Hilton to use their pools- we used and just well worth having a look at this complex complete with its own monorail!! We had a rental to do some day touring and beach visits. While there is a food store at Queen's its expensive so a short drive (15 mins) to the larger store at Waikoloa Village well worth it. Eat out options average at Queens and the nearby Kings Market Places, but we found Sansei Seafood, Steak and Sushi Bar at Queens superb - but you need to book. Most bars have happy hour (50% on beers and house wines from 3-6). We found beach front Lava Lava Beach Club by far the best here for ambiance, drinks and food-try the pulled pork sliders! and the marvellous sunset too and turtles came ashore  for the night. Hapuna Beach the best but need to take own chairs and umbrellas (from the garage). We did an 11 hour day trip with tour company to other side of island to see the volcanoes - much of the flora and fauna shown we have in NZ  but the lava glow/aura we saw at night was stunning. Trip was expensive but included a lunch and seated dinner - value for money ?? but we went to see the volcanoes and weren't disappointed.  Discount available if you want to sit through a Hilton presentation (no thanks).\nWe've been fortunate to travel worldly. In terms of relaxation this was the best. Two weeks without rain and 29-32 deg temps - heaven!   We're already planning a return in 2018! Just leave us a 10 day window please!"},{"_id":"212171514","date":"2017-11-16T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"8543198","reviewer_id":"112750315","reviewer_name":"Carol And Shawn","comments":"This place was as described and was a fantastic place to call home for a week. Getting to and from the city centre of Porto takes some time. There are several buslines (and a historic tram) but one has to be patient. A rented bike is usefull, for exploring the coast or riding along the river (Vueguini rental). It takes 1,5 hrs to get with a rented car to from Helena's place to the interesting parts of the Douro valley and vinyards. On walking distance is the Foundation Serralves, museum and garden. Very nice!\nThanks for having us, Helena! The view from upstairs is lovely. Short walk to the beach, where sea turtles and monk seals hang out and don't seem to be bothered by people. The house is huge! There were 7 of us total and the house had more than enough space and beds. Two families could easily share this rental and be happy and comfortable. The upstairs and downstairs of the house are almost separate 2bd/1ba units. It had been professionally cleaned prior to our arrival. There are boogie boards, snorkel gear and beach chairs in the garage, which was very useful for us. The kitchen is stocked with some basics and you're set up to run to the grocery store and make meals at the house, if you want. There are even gas and charcoal grills and outdoor picnic tables for your use, if you want them. We chose to do breakfast at home, then eat out for all lunches and dinners, since there's a lot to try on the island. The only downside is that the rental was fairly expensive, but since my family and I had a great time, in the end I think it was worth the cost. We had six (four adults, two kids) and everyone was happy!"},{"_id":"319568086","date":"2018-09-06T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"3270926","reviewer_id":"58415706","reviewer_name":"Shannon","comments":"The Turtle Suites is a massive condo/home in an amazing location in Poipu.  It is literally across the street from Brenneke's beach and up a small short lane.  Poipu Beach and Brennekes were within walking distance and we walked to them everyday multiple times.  Other guests left chairs, umbrella, boogie boards and sand toys in the garage so we were able to use them at the beach.  There was so much space to spread out in the unit and relax.  There are actually three official bedrooms as listed but a fourth sleeping area/room with a double bed and a twin trundle underneath that can be partitioned off by an accordian (Website hidden by Airbnb) there are actual beds for ten with at least six futons that can be slept on as well.  There are two 'family rooms' with large HD televisions and a great kitchen space.  We had views of the ocean from both bedrooms upstairs as well as the upstairs and downstairs lanais.  Another review said that there was only one working shower downstairs but the upstairs shower works fine it just has a different way of turning the water from the faucet to the shower.  There is a ring around the opening of the faucet where the water comes out that you have to pull down to transfer water from tub to shower.  :)  There are two grills outside the garages with picnic tables on the grass.  We used the grill that was basically brand new (garages are a separate building from the home)  Be aware that the pool, hot tub, bball courts, workout space, pickleball courts are not right next to the property but down the road a mile...and it closes at 7.  That was a bit disappointing but the home was not.  Before you go to the store to buy seasonings and sauces check out the cupboard and drawer between the fridge and microwave...there are tons of them in the home to use.  There were tons of pots and pans, two toasters, a blender and coffee maker (we did not use this tho).  There was not any big bowl or glass baking dishes to use.  We have been burned several times by airbnb's before so were so pleased with this location.  You will be amazed at how large it is and the location is awesome.  I am very impressed by the speed of communication each time I had a question.  Check in and out were a breeze."},{"_id":"323099350","date":"2018-09-14T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"3270926","reviewer_id":"28291647","reviewer_name":"Helen","comments":"We were very happy with the Turtle Suite. Carlos was very responsive to my initial inquiry and to all subsequent inquiries about the house.\r\n\r\nAlthough Carlos was out of town, he arranged for Vitor to be available to us during the rental.  Vitor was very helpful.  We had to open some locked windows and Vitor came within an hour to fix the problem.  Also, we had a hot water issue, but again Vitor was at the house and fixed the problem immediately (so fast I didn't have a chance to read his response email - he arrived before it did!).  These issues happen and the most important thing is to get them fixed as quickly as possible.  I was impressed with the level of responsiveness.\r\n\r\nThe house is well designed and charming.  The pictures are accurate - the house is beautiful.  The beds are very comfortable.  We used all the appliances and all worked.  There are plenty of pots and pans and sufficient dishes, glasses and cutlery.  We bought fish at the Bolhao market and had a great dinner at home one night in the dining room that we cooked in the kitchen of the house. The internet was also fine.\r\n\r\nThe host supplied a decent baby bed and a very good high chair for the baby.  The house was very clean upon arrival.  The locks work well, but are tricky for North Americans.  Be sure to try them with the host present.\r\n\r\nIt isn't clear from the pictures or description, but there are multiple levels to the house all reached via a spiral staircase in the middle.  There is one double bedroom on the ground floor that has its own 2 piece bathroom.  People using this room have to go upstairs to someone else's bathroom to bathe or shower.  (The other two bedrooms have beautiful ensuite full bathrooms). This was not a problem for us at all.  There is also one other 1/2 bathroom in the house.\r\n\r\nThis house is in a very residential neighbourhood but in the old part of town.  It's about a 10 minute walk to the restaurants along the riverside.  We walked to the port houses from here - about 20 minutes walk with a great view of the river the whole way (and we were pushing a stroller).  There are a couple of good neighbourhood cafes very close by and a small grocery store a few metres away where we could buy meat, cheese, wine, milk etc. - limited selection, but all the necessities are available.  The location is reasonably quiet at night too.  It's a good location to be in to feel as if you are living like a local but close enough to walk to the main sights or catch a bus if necessary.  The tram to the beach at Foz do Douro stops nearby as well.\r\n\r\nI would stay here again."},{"_id":"38316529","date":"2015-07-14T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"6868273","reviewer_id":"21307293","reviewer_name":"Marcus","comments":"Carlos was super friendly and helpful.
